from.place: proof: cut a perfect complex after the degree-zero fibre map is surjective

title: Affine perfect-complex cut after a surjective fibre map
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, let p be a prime ideal of R, and let K be a bounded-above complex of finite free R-modules. Assume that the canonical map H^0(K) tensor_R kappa(p) to H^0(K tensor_R^L kappa(p)) [def-pc-module-cohomology-base-change] is surjective. Then there is f not in p such that, in the derived category D(R_f), K tensor_R R_f is isomorphic to tau_{<=0}(K tensor_R R_f) direct-sum tau_{>=1}(K tensor_R R_f), and tau_{>=1}(K tensor_R R_f) is represented by a bounded complex of finite projective R_f-modules in degrees at least 1; in particular tau_{>=1}(K tensor_R R_f) is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] of Tor-amplitude in [1,infinity).

proof.text: Write kappa for kappa(p). By the bounded-above finite-free hypothesis, inspect the three consecutive terms K^{−1} to K^0 to K^1. In K^0 tensor_R kappa define V as the image of K^{−1} tensor_R kappa and W as the kernel of K^0 tensor_R kappa to K^1 tensor_R kappa. Choose x_a in K^{−1} whose differentials form a basis of V, choose y_b in Ker(d^0) mapping to a basis of W/V using the assumed surjectivity of H^0(K) tensor_R kappa to H^0(K tensor_R^L kappa), and choose z_c in K^0 lifting a basis of (K^0 tensor_R kappa)/W. Then the d^0(z_c) are linearly independent in K^1 tensor_R kappa.

Let $\psi:R^{\oplus(r+s+t)}\to K^0$ send the standard basis to the elements $d^{-1}(x_a),y_b,z_c$. Its residue-field map is an isomorphism, so the isomorphism clause of [lem-pc-finite-projective-cokernel-localization] gives, after shrinking by $f\notin\mathfrak p$, that these elements form an $R_f$-basis of $(K^0)_f$. Apply the injective-fibre clause of the same node to $R^{\oplus t}\to K^1$, sending the standard basis to $d^0(z_c)$; after a further shrinking, these elements are $R_f$-linearly independent and their cokernel $E^1$ is finite projective. Since $d^0$ kills $d^{-1}(x_a)$ and $y_b$, $E^1=\operatorname{Coker}(d^0)$. Thus $\tau_{\geq1}(K^\bullet\otimes_RR_f)$ is represented by the bounded complex with $E^1$ in degree $1$ and the original finite free terms in higher degrees (bounded because $K$ is bounded above), hence by finite projectives in degrees $[1,b]$ for some $b$. Such a complex is strictly perfect on $\operatorname{Spec}(R_f)$, so $\tau_{\geq1}(K^\bullet\otimes_RR_f)$ is perfect; its terms are flat and vanish below degree $1$, so tensoring with any $R_f$-module has no cohomology below degree $1$, i.e. its Tor-amplitude is in $[1,\infty)$.

The truncation triangle tau_{<=0}(K tensor_R R_f) to K tensor_R R_f to tau_{>=1}(K tensor_R R_f) to tau_{<=0}(K tensor_R R_f)[1] is distinguished. The right-hand object has projective-amplitude in [1,b] for some b, while the left-hand object has no cohomology in degrees greater than 0. The derived splitting statement [lem-pc-derived-splitting-unique], with a=1, therefore supplies a canonical direct-sum isomorphism K tensor_R R_f isomorphic to tau_{<=0}(K tensor_R R_f) direct-sum tau_{>=1}(K tensor_R R_f).
